record.title: MiMo-V2.6 reports large-scale mixed-harness reinforcement learning for agents
record.summary: An Oct. 8 technical report describes Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro and Flash models and a mixed-task agentic reinforcement-learning system spanning coding, general workflows, visual tasks, and cybersecurity. The authors report 1,568 prompts with 16 rollouts each per training step, 2.7–3.7 billion tokens per step, and 30-step runs costing about $2.6 million for Pro and $0.9 million for Flash. They report DeepSWE v1.1 average@3 rising from 58.4 to 72.6 for Pro and 48.7 to 65.7 for Flash, and held-out coding harness Pass@1 improving from about 50% to 66%. The report also describes a released 9B distilled model, task environments, and an RL framework. These are author-reported results; no independent reproduction or cost audit was performed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: arXiv lists the Xiaomi LLM-Core Team's MiMo-V2.6 technical report as submitted on 8 October 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report asynchronous mixed-task agentic RL using 1,568 prompts and 16 rollouts per step, consuming 2.7–3.7 billion tokens per step; their Pro and Flash runs are described as 30 steps with costs of about $2.6 million and $0.9 million, respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report DeepSWE v1.1 average@3 increasing over RL from 58.4 to 72.6 for Pro and 48.7 to 65.7 for Flash, and mean Pass@1 rising from about 50% to 66% on three held-out coding harnesses.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The report states that Xiaomi released a 9B distilled model, RL environments and verifiers, and an end-to-end RL framework; the research desk did not inspect the artifacts or confirm their completeness in this activation.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported benchmark trajectories, held-out harness transfer, or 9B gains has been completed.
The report's RL costs and shared infrastructure accounting have not been independently audited.
The claimed open resources have not been audited artifact-by-artifact for availability, versioning, verifiers, and license scope.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported mixed-harness RL recipe and training gains reproduce, the combination of very large asynchronous rollout batches, diverse long-horizon environments, groupwise grading, and a released smaller-model research stack could materially change how frontier agent post-training is organized and evaluated. The reported training costs and gains remain vendor-authored and have not been independently reproduced, so the consequence is major rather than established field change.
brief.summary: An Oct. 8 technical report describes Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro and Flash models and a mixed-task agentic reinforcement-learning system spanning coding, general workflows, visual tasks, and cybersecurity. The authors report 1,568 prompts with 16 rollouts each per training step, 2.7–3.7 billion tokens per step, and 30-step runs costing about $2.6 million for Pro and $0.9 million for Flash. They report DeepSWE v1.1 average@3 rising from 58.4 to 72.6 for Pro and 48.7 to 65.7 for Flash, and held-out coding harness Pass@1 improving from about 50% to 66%. The report also describes a released 9B distilled model, task environments, and an RL framework. These are author-reported results; no independent reproduction or cost audit was performed.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report 1,568 prompts x 16 rollouts (about 25,000 sequences) and 2.7–3.7B tokens per step; 30-step RL runs costing about $2.6M for Pro and $0.9M for Flash; DeepSWE v1.1 average@3 increasing from 58.4 to 72.6 (Pro) and 48.7 to 65.7 (Flash); and mean Pass@1 on three held-out coding harnesses increasing from about 50% to 66%. For the 9B distilled model, they report SWE-bench Pro from 32.0 to 44.6 and AutomationBench from 5.0% to 30.3% after supervised distillation and separate RL experiments.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary report documents the described training and evaluation setup and publishes author-reported measurements. the research desk did not reproduce the training, independently audit the cost accounting, verify the benchmarks, or inspect the released artifacts in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The report combines asynchronous large-batch RL over code, general-agent, visual, and cybersecurity environments with multiple agent harnesses. It describes Groupwise Reward Synthesis and Groupwise Advantage Redistribution for richer grading, a frozen MoE router for training stability, rollout scheduling and replay infrastructure, and a defense process for reward hacking. A separate open research stack uses a distilled 9B model, released environments and verifiers, and an end-to-end training framework.
technical.regime: Xiaomi-authored report on two proprietary MoE model variants and one 9B distilled model. The main RL results span provider-selected coding, general-agent, visual, and cybersecurity tasks; multi-harness transfer is reported for coding, with three held-out harnesses. The open 9B experiments use released resources but are separate from the full Pro and Flash runs.
technical.strongest_baseline: The report compares progression across its own 30-step RL runs and includes an author-run router-freezing contrast plus three held-out coding harnesses. No independent matched-cost baseline or replication was conducted.

brief.title: MiMo-V2.6 reports large-scale mixed-harness reinforcement learning for agents
brief.why_it_matters: This report makes large-scale, long-horizon agentic RL more inspectable by tying training scale, harness diversity, reward grading, failure modes, and an open smaller-model stack to one described system. If the reported cross-harness and benchmark gains reproduce, they could inform how labs allocate post-training compute and construct agent environments. The run costs, provider-designed benchmarks, and absence of independent reproduction leave the size and transferability of the gains uncertain.
